themes.title: Barrel and tree-shaking shape
themes.question: What does a consumer who imports one Button actually download, and does the barrel in src/index.ts plus package.json sideEffects let the rest be shaken out?
themes.notes: Ranked #1: surfaces join to the whole export table (barrel totalBytes 145,597 B gz, the largest measured surface). Verdict: per-export tree-shaking WORKS. sideEffects:['**/*.css'] is effectively false for the JS graph (no .ts/.tsx imports .css); preserveModules emits one dist file per module; @base-ui via subpaths; lucide per-icon; type-only imports erased; ogl reachable ONLY via the Aurora export (aurora.tsx imported by no other non-story module); seasons decoupled from chrome (import type). The one cross-cutting gap = no per-component subpath exports despite dist already emitting the files -> RSC/imperfect bundlers traverse the whole barrel. Filed #52. Deferred to sibling themes: (a) ogl as a hard `dependency` vs optional peer = install-weight, belongs to ogl-reachability; (b) the ~8.5 KB tailwind-merge/clsx `cn` floor is counted per-export in the snapshot but deduped in real apps, so it is a reading caveat, not a defect (not filed, would be a false positive).

themes.title: ogl reachability from the main entry
themes.question: Is the WebGL dependency reachable from the package entry point, and can it move behind a lazy or split path so consumers who never render Aurora do not pay for it?
themes.notes: The bundle snapshot records reachable externals per export — check it before reasoning about the module graph by hand.

themes.title: Animation loop policy across every driven component
themes.question: Do all rAF, WebGL, and timer loops honour prefers-reduced-motion, pause on visibilitychange, and stop when off-screen? Treat this as one policy, not as a per-file question.
themes.notes: vrt/skip.json documents that Aurora's loop is free-running and does not honour prefers-reduced-motion. Fixing that also makes the component baseline-able, which closes a VRT coverage hole.

themes.title: Resource disposal sweep
themes.question: Does every GPU resource, timer, observer, and listener have a teardown path on unmount?
themes.notes: The bench CANNOT help with this theme yet: retention is measured but uncalibrated, so every verdict is 'unknown' and the raw slopes track story size rather than leaks. Disposal must be argued from the teardown code itself. Do not quote a retention number as evidence of a leak.

themes.title: Re-render cascade mapping
themes.question: Where does a parent re-render cascade across component boundaries, and which context values or prop identities cause it?
themes.notes: Ranked #1: surfaces join to the most expensive component exports (BoardSelector 73,530 B gz — largest single component; LanguageSelector 60,142; Sidebar 57,492) and the highest-mount bench stories (chrome-appshell--collapsed 55.5ms, chrome-sidebar--ai-active 52.7ms, board-scaledboarddisplay 47.1ms). VERDICT: RESOLVED at the library level — nothing new to file. This theme was already investigated in a prior run and filed as #63 (CLOSED/COMPLETED, not rejected; rejected-findings.jsonl is empty), whose fixes are all present in the current tree: (a) every chrome component is now memo'd — sidebar, board-selector, language-selector, theme-toggle, main-content, page-header/page-layout/page-toolbar, fiesta-logo, board-icon; (b) the Select context churn is stabilized via lib/select-items stabilizeSelectItems + render-phase state adjustment (#62), so SelectItemsContext value and Base UI `items` stay referentially stable; (c) Sidebar's window-resize appInset listener is now rAF-coalesced and bails when the inset is unchanged (sidebar.tsx:275-296), and the ResizeObserver header-height publish is likewise coalesced + skips unchanged writes. The board render path is triple-protected against cascades: BoardDisplay + CharTile + GridRow + StaticGridRow + StaticTile all memo'd with custom comparators; the grid array is useMemo'd and rows are reference-stable so a BoardDisplay re-render does not reach the tiles; flapSpeed is compared via resolveFlapSpeed so a fresh {durationMs} object does not re-render; loading uses one shared ticker per cadence instead of ~132 per-tile intervals; board-surfaces.ts materials and board-metrics class maps are module-scope. The seasonal auroras (SidebarAurora/SidebarAuroraHorizontal, rendered directly by Sidebar) are memo'd on a stable `colors` ref. The ONLY residual cascade is consumer-side prop identity: the memo #63 added to the chrome shell only bails if the consuming app passes referentially-stable slot/array/render-prop values (Sidebar.boardSelector/mobileBoardSelector/versionSlot/themeToggleSlot/primaryItems/secondaryItems/renderLink/ai, MainContent.children). At the AppShell demo composition these are recreated on every shell state change, so memo does not bail — but that is not a library defect (a presentational/controlled library cannot stabilize consumer-supplied identities) and #63 explicitly deferred it as the separate discovered theme `prop-contract-stability`. Not refiled: doing so would re-propose a finding #63 already deferred AND belongs to the 'memo'd component + unstable consumer props' false-positive class. Considered and rejected as a finding: ScaledBoardDisplay uses React's default shallow memo while wrapping the custom-comparator BoardDisplay — this is the normal memo pattern (stable for the default flapSpeed='standard'/no-custom-label case) and BoardDisplay's comparator backstops the tiles regardless, so it is not a defect.

themes.title: CSS paint and layer budget
themes.question: Which styles promote layers, force paint, or use unbounded will-change, and what does that cost across the whole stylesheet rather than per component?
themes.notes: Large blur radii and layer promotion show up in the bench as frame p95 above the vsync floor.

themes.title: Prop-contract stability for the presentational shell
themes.question: Now that the chrome shell is uniformly memo'd (#63), its memos only bail when the consuming app passes referentially-stable slot/array/render-prop values — which the documented AppShell composition does not. Should the library close this at its own boundary (a composed AppShell that owns stable slot/callback identities, and/or a stabilization hook) rather than leaving every consumer to hand-memoize, and what does the un-bailed cascade actually cost per shell state change?
themes.notes:
Ranked #1 by measured surface cost: chrome/** + forms/select.tsx join to the most expensive exports (BoardSelector 73,382 B gz, Combobox/TimezonePicker aside, LanguageSelector 59,934, Select 58,913, Sidebar 54,530) and the highest-MOUNT bench stories (app-chrome-appshell--collapsed 57.5ms, app-chrome-sidebar--ai-active 54ms, app-chrome-boardselector--collapsed 43.2ms, app-chrome-languageselector--default 42.1ms). The other four pending themes (ogl-reachability, animation-loop-policy, resource-disposal, css-paint-budget) rank far below: no Aurora/Season/ogl export appears in snapshot-bundle.json AT ALL and the barrel externals no longer list ogl, and src/components/seasons + src/components/effects are absent/empty, so those three surfaces carry ZERO measured bundle cost and no measured bench story (only effects-react-bits-fadecontent--default, 31.6ms). css-paint-budget (styles/**) maps to no export and every frame p95 sits at the 16.7ms vsync floor.

VERDICT: NO LIBRARY-SIDE DEFECT. Filed 0 issues; recommend a human PRUNE this theme. Full surface sweep (sidebar.tsx, main-content.tsx, board-selector.tsx, language-selector.tsx, theme-toggle.tsx, page-header.tsx, page-layout.tsx, page-toolbar.tsx, page-inset.tsx, forms/select.tsx, lib/select-items.ts) confirms every chrome component is correctly memo'd (#63) with NO internal identity churn: render-invariant style objects are module-hoisted (page-toolbar TOOLBAR_STYLE, page-header DEFS_SVG_STYLE), BoardSelector useMemo's its SelectItem list, and Select uses the content-keyed stabilization from #62 (stabilizeSelectItems + render-phase state adjustment) so SelectItemsContext value and Base UI `items` stay referentially stable across re-renders. The residual 'un-bailed cascade' is ENTIRELY consumer-supplied prop identity in the app-shell.stories.tsx demo, where a single AppShellDemo owns collapsed/theme/board and recreates every slot (<BoardSelector/>, <ThemeToggle/>, versionSlot), array (boards, primary, secondaryItems) and callback (onToggleCollapsed, onChange, onToggle) inline per render.

Why this is NOT fileable against the library: (1) NO MEASURED EVIDENCE exists — the bench is mount-only (selection.mode one-per-component, no interaction/update pass), so the 54-57ms sidebar/appshell numbers are MOUNT cost (Base UI Select/Tooltip construction), not re-render cost; any cascade cost is reasoned, not measured. (2) For the shell's signature interaction, COLLAPSE, memoization is irrelevant: Sidebar, MainContent and BoardSelector all genuinely consume `collapsed`, so a toggle MUST re-render all three — no memo boundary could bail regardless of prop identity. (3) The only cascade a memo could prevent (theme/board change re-rendering the nav list) is a STORY ARTIFACT: the demo hoists all three states into one component for brevity; a real integration scopes theme/current-board in separate providers so board selection never reaches the nav. Even the strongest real-consumer case (collapsed lives in a common ancestor of Sidebar+MainContent, so a toggle recreates the sibling slots) yields only trivial needless re-renders of ThemeToggle (one Button + 3 icons) and versionSlot (a span) on a rare user click. (4) A presentational, fully-controlled shell CANNOT stabilize identities that are inherently consumer-owned application state (theme, board, onChange). A composed <AppShell> or useAppShellState hook could own only chrome-only state (collapsed/transitioning; Sidebar already owns mobileMenuOpen internally) — it would remove ~6 lines of consumer boilerplate but NOT reduce the cascade, because the slots still carry consumer state and the composed shell would itself re-render and recreate them. That is an ergonomics/DX proposal, not a perf fix. Filing 'memoize your props' or 'ship an AppShell for perf' here is exactly the false-positive class the prior note flagged. Considered-and-rejected minor items (both daily-sweep territory, visible in one file, negligible): Select re-runs collectSelectItems + selectItemsContentKey (a bounded React.Children walk) on every render — the deliberate, accepted correctness tradeoff of #62 for small option sets; PageHeader allocates a fresh style={{animationDelay}} object per render but is memo'd and default '0ms'. Dedupe: no open perf-explore or perf-audit issue matched; nothing to comment on.
